chunks: And from him, from al-Nadhr, from Ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the saying of Allah, the Exalted: 'So pray to your Lord and sacrifice.' He said: 'It is the raising of your hands to the level of your face.'

key_terms.وَانْحَرْ: And sacrifice (referring to the ritual raising of hands)

ai.seo_question: What does the command 'fasalli li-rabbika wanhar' in Surah Al-Kawthar refer to in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the phrase 'wa inhar' (and sacrifice) in Surah Al-Kawthar is interpreted not merely as slaughter, but as the physical act of raising the hands (raf' al-yadayn) to the level of the face during prayer. This interpretation highlights the connection between the ritual gesture of takbir and the concept of devotion and sacrifice, a view supported by Shia scholars who link the linguistic root of 'inhar' to the lifting of hands in supplication.
